timed_text.text: day 27. I want to leave you with a question that I want you to carry for the rest of your career.
What's next? Not what did I achieve? What's next? Here's why this matters. One of the biggest
performance killers in sport is complacency after success. You achieve something, you make the team,
you get the starting spot, you hit a personal best, and without realizing it,
your standards quietly drop. Because part of your brain thinks the job is done.
The what's next habit prevents that. It builds the mindset of continuous growth.
Of setting new limits the moment you reach the old ones. Of understanding that achievement is
not a destination, it's a direction. The athletes who sustain elite performance over years and
seasons are not the ones who were satisfied with what they built. They were the ones who used
each achievement as a launching pad for the next standard. You're three days from completing
this whole program. And the most important thing that can tell you is this. Finishing is not the goal.
The next chapter is on your screen. You're going to answer the prompted question.

cards.prompt: What have you built over the last 27 days that you didn't have when you started?
What is the next standard you're committing to? Not a wish — a specific, behavioral commitment that starts the day after this program ends.
What's next? Write it as a declaration. 'After this program, I commit to...'

timed_text.text: Every achievement, every season, every milestone.
The answer to that question is where the growth lives.
Now that you're finished, day 27 is complete.
